==English== ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱerd-|*dʰeh₁-}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|crédit||belief, trust}}, from {{der|en|la|crēditum||a loan, credit}}, neuter of {{m|la|crēditus}}, past participle of {{m|la|crēdere||to believe}}. The verb is from the noun. {{doublet|en|shraddha}}, {{m|en|creed}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈkɹɛdɪt/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-credit.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛdɪt|s=2}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[believe]]; to put [[credence]] in. {{attn|en|British usage?}} #: {{syn|en|accept|believe}} #: {{ux|en|Someone said there were over 100,000 people there, but I can't '''credit''' that.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare All's Well|I|iii|passage=How shall they '''credit'''
A poor unlearned virgin?}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1777|author=w:Richard Brinsley Sheridan|title=The School for Scandal|section=IV.iii |passage=[T]he Heart that is conscious of its own integrity is ever slowest to '''credit''' another's Treachery.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1952|author=w:Daphne du Maurier|title=The Apple Tree|chapter=Monte Verità|passage=She said quite naturally, as if nothing had happened, “I want you to go back home, Victor darling. You mustn’t worry about me any more.”’ Victor told me he could hardly '''credit''' it, at first, that she could stand there and say this to him.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|accounting}} To add to an account. #: {{antonyms|en|debit}} #: {{ux|en|'''Credit''' accounts receivable with the amount of the invoice.}} #: {{ux|en|For the payroll period '''credit''' employees' tips to their wages paid account and debit their minimum wage payable account.}} #: {{ux|en|The full amount of the purchase has been '''credited''' to your account.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To acknowledge the contribution of. #: {{ux|en|I '''credit''' the town council with restoring the shopping district.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Credit''' the point guard with another assist.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:Architectural Digest|date=May 2026|volume=83|issue=4|title=Nature's Way|author=Cyrus Dunham|page=106 |text=So sublime was the region that many '''credit''' it with being the birthplace of British tourism.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To bring honour or repute upon; to do credit to; to raise the estimation of. #* {{RQ:South Twelve Sermons|passage=You '''credit''' the church as much by your government as you did the school formerly by your wit.}} ====Conjugation==== {{en-conj|old=1}} ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|discredit|miscredit|recredit|uncredit}} ====Related terms==== {{col3|en|credible |credibility |creditable |creditor |creditworthy |credence |credential |credo |creed }} ====Translations==== {{trans-top-see|to believe|accredit|give credit|believe}} * Bulgarian: * Chinese: * Dutch: * Finnish: * German: * Hungarian: * Indonesian: * Italian: * Korean: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|ве́рить|impf}}, {{t+|ru|пове́рить|pf}}, {{t+|ru|доверя́ть|impf}}, {{t+|ru|дове́рить|pf}} * Serbo-Croatian: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to add to an account}} * Czech: * Dutch: * Finnish: * German: * Hungarian: * Indonesian: * Italian: * Norwegian: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|зачислять|impf|pf}} * Swedish: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top-see|to acknowledge a contribution|accredit|give credit|acknowledge|attribute}} * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Dutch: * Finnish: * German: * Hungarian: * Indonesian: * Italian: * Naga: * Russian: {{t+|ru|припи́сывать|impf}}, {{t+|ru|приписа́ть|pf}} * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun|~}} # Reliance on the truth of something said or done; faith; trust. #* {{RQ:KJV|1 Maccabees|10|46|passage=When Jonathan and the people heard these words they gave no '''credit''' into them, nor received them.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[recognition|Recognition]], [[respect]] and [[admiration]]. #: {{syn|en|due}} #: {{ux|en|I give you '''credit''' for owning up to your mistake.}} #: {{ux|en|He arrived five minutes late, but to his '''credit''' he did work an extra ten minutes at the end of his shift.}} #* {{RQ:Cowper John Gilpin|page=343|passage=John Gilpin was a citizen
Of '''credit''' and renown,
A train-band Captain eke was he
Of famous London town.}} #* {{quote-web|en|date=December 10, 2011|author=David Ornstein quoting {{w|David Moyes}}|title=Arsenal 1 - 0 Everton|work=w:BBC Sport|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/16015017.stm|passage="I've got to give '''credit''' to Van Persie, it was a great goal. We didn't mean to give them chances but they're a good team."|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120107113248/http://news.bbc.co.uk:80/sport2/hi/football/16015017.stm|archivedate=7 January 2012}} # {{lb|en|countable}} Acknowledgement of a contribution, especially in the [[performing arts]]. #: {{ux|en|She received a singing '''credit''' in last year's operetta.}} #* {{quote-journal|en |date=November 1 2020 |url=https://www.scotsman.com/arts-and-culture/film-and-tv/sean-connery-obituary-delivering-milk-fountainbridge-definitive-james-bond-3021133 |author=Alan Young |work=The Scotsman |title=His first major acting '''credit''' came in 1957 British gangster film No Road Back. |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230223020345/https://www.scotsman.com/arts-and-culture/film-and-tv/sean-connery-obituary-delivering-milk-fountainbridge-definitive-james-bond-3021133 |archivedate=23 February 2023 }} # {{lb|en|television|film|usually|in the plural}} Written [[title]]s and other information about the TV program or movie shown at the beginning and/or end of the TV program or movie. #: {{ux|en|They kissed, and then the '''credits''' rolled.}} # {{senseid|en|Q182076}} {{lb|en|uncountable|law|business|finance}} A privilege of delayed payment extended to a buyer or borrower on the seller's or lender's belief that what is given will be repaid. #: {{ux|en|In view of your payment record, we are happy to extend further '''credit''' to you.}} # The time given for payment for something sold on trust. #: {{ux|en|a long '''credit''' or a short '''credit'''}} # {{lb|en|uncountable|US}} A person's [[credit rating]] or [[creditworthiness]], as represented by their history of borrowing and repayment (or non payment). #: {{ux|en|What do you mean my '''credit''' is no good?}} # {{lb|en|accounting}} An addition to certain accounts; the side of an account on which payments received are entered. # {{lb|en|tax accounting}} A reduction in taxes owed, or a refund for excess taxes paid. #: {{ux|en|Didn't you know that the IRS will refund any excess payroll taxes that you paid if you use the 45(B) general business '''credit'''?}} # A source of [[value]], [[distinction]] or [[honour]]. #: {{ux|en|That engineer is a '''credit''' to the team.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1836|author=w:Henry Francis Cary|title=The Poetical Works of Alexander Pope.: The Author's Preface |passage=I published, because I was told I might please such as it was a '''credit''' to please.}} # {{lb|en|science fiction}} A unit of [[currency]] used in a fictional universe or timeframe. #: {{ux|en|To repair your star cruiser will cost 100,000 '''credits'''.}} #* {{quote-video game|en|developer=w:BioWare|title={{w|Mass Effect (video game)|Mass Effect}}|location=Redwood City|publisher=Electronic Arts|year=2008|system=PC|scene=Credits ("Creds") Codex entry|isbn=9780784546642|oclc=246633669|passage=The standard '''credit''' was established by the Citadel's Unified Banking Act as the currency of interstellar trade. The '''credit''' has a managed floating exchange rate, calculated in real time by the central bank to maintain the average value of all participating currencies. Some regional currencies are worth more than a '''credit''' and some less.}} # A nominal unit of value assigned outside of a currency system. #: {{ux|en|Would you like to play? I put in a dollar and I've got two '''credits''' left.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} Recognition for having taken a course (class). #: {{ux|en|If you do not come to class, you will not get '''credit''' for the class, regardless of how well you do on the final.}} # {{lb|en|countable}} A {{w|course credit}}, a credit hour – used as measure if enough courses have been taken for graduation. #:
